_doc: The hideout's line shack (#1091, Sean 2026-11-25): Kett's cabin in No Justice. Written by experiments/building_lab/line_shack/gen_spec.py (never by hand); its plan and the walk are that folder's README.

identity.owner: nobody's now: an old cow-camp line shack of a range outfit that went under; Kett's crew (five men) hole up in it between jobs
identity.trade: the gang's hideout: they sleep, eat, drink, play cards and keep their saddles and kit here
identity.means: nothing spent on it: whatever was left, patched with what was to hand
identity.age_and_repair: raised about 1872 of mill boards hauled in by wagon: the boards silver-grey and brown, warped, gapped, a few split; tin cans flattened and nailed over holes; shakes curled and a patch slipped
clues: two bunks stacked and a third, more men than beds (bedrolls on the floor)
a deck of cards on the table
saddles in the lean-to and one inside
a bar and brackets on the door: they expected company

lot._doc: The hideout's pad (valley.json `hideout`: at [-450, 2020], 30 x 20 m, y 86). `at` the west front corner's world point: the moment's `shack.at` [7, 5] off the pad's at, less half the shack. The mission (no_justice_hideout.gd `_build_shack`) loads this spec and sets it on the ground's high corner as now.
lot._footprint: the room and the storeroom behind it (6.5 m deep in all; its back 9.0 m south of the pad's at, inside the pad's 10)

levels._doc: One storey: the floor 0.32 m up on sleepers over the sills; the walls to a plate at 2.6 m; an 8/12 shake roof gabled front to back (the ridge north-south), its rakes 0.3 m past the gables, the eaves 0.3 m out.

frame._doc: A light box frame on sills on flat stones: corner posts, studs at 24 in, a girt halfway up, rough boards and battens outside, no inside finish (the frame shows); sleepers and a girder under the floor; rafters, collars, skip boards, shakes.

foundation._doc: flat sandstone slabs under the corners and every 1.2 m, not a run of wall (the gaps under the sill dark)

sill._doc: 4x6 on the flat, halved at the corners

girder._doc: a 4x6 down the middle under the sleepers (2.05 m spans either side)

joist._doc: 2x6 sleepers at 24 in on the sills and girder (5 crew and a crowd's check)

rafters._doc: 2x4 at 24 in over 2.1 m runs, a collar on every pair 0.5 m under the ridge (no ceiling joists: the room open to the shakes)

floors._doc: rough 1x8 boards across the sleepers; the board at the door the sill's threshold (flush: nothing to trip on)

shakes._doc: split shakes 8 in to the weather on skip boards a foot apart; a patch slipped off the west slope over Kett's corner (light through it)

walls._doc: the north gable: the one door, in its middle (x 2.1, the stand-in's), the doorstep before it

openings._doc: a batten door (four 1x10 planks on two battens and a Z-brace, strap hinges on the west jamb, swinging in to the west wall); the bar a 2x4 dropped into two iron brackets on the jambs (the cabin's `front/door_bar`); kicked in it breaks along its planks: flat 25 mm boards, nothing a man must climb (#1091's must: Joe never stalls on the sill)

walls._doc: the south gable, toward the canyon side: the storeroom's door at the lane's end, the storeroom built against it; tin patches over two holes (the storeroom's walls)

openings._doc: into the storeroom: a low plank door on leather hinges, a wooden latch, no bar (he pulls it to behind him; a kick or E opens it); swinging into the storeroom against its west wall, so Kett crouches behind its leaf

walls._doc: the long side to the slope (where you come down from): no openings
the long side to the horses: the one window over the single bunk, the lean-to against it

openings._doc: four dirty lights, one cracked; a plank shutter hung open beside it

outbuildings._doc: the back storeroom (Sean, 2026-11-25): a closed lean-to across the south gable, its shed roof falling south from a ledger under the gable, its floor the shack's level, no window (dark: light only through the board gaps and its door). Sacks, crates, a keg, spare tack. Kett hides here. The builder's lean_to as the farmhouse's (closed), its siding the shack's.

an open pole lean-to against the east wall: a ledger on the studs under the eave, poles from it to a pole beam on two juniper posts, old boards across; dirt under; open at the north, east and south (NEW in the builder: `open`, `posts`, `floor: dirt`)

doorstep._doc: The stand-in's flat stone before the door (#966), now a sandstone slab: half the floor's height, so two 0.16 m steps.

list._doc: a 6 in tin pipe up from the box stove through a tin plate in the east slope near the ridge's back, a coolie cap, three guy wires

rooms.use: the crew's stores and spare tack; where Kett hides when the door is forced (#1091, Sean 2026-11-25)
five men sleep, eat, drink and keep their kit in the one room; Kett is barred in here at the end (No Justice, #966)

kept_clear._doc: the storeroom's west half bare: Kett's hiding place behind its door's leaf, nothing he or Joe or the knife can catch on (the stores stand in its east half)
the lane from the door to the storeroom's door: 0.9-1.0 m between the stacked bunks and the table's west bench, to the back wall; nothing stands in it
where the kicked-in door's planks fall (`door_falls_mps` 0.8 inward): flat boards only, the floor otherwise bare

use_points._doc: PROPOSED for no_justice_cabin.json `corner` (now [0.75, 4.3]): where Kett hides, in the storeroom behind its door's leaf, facing the door. `in_shack` must count the storeroom (the shack's depth 6.5 m, or the spec's rooms)
PROPOSED for the cabin's `joe_in` (now [3.3, 1.5], east of the door: the table and the single bunk would stand in his way to Kett); in the west lane, past the door's fall
PROPOSED for `joe_back` (now [2.9, 0.8]): the same, back by the door

walk._doc: Joe's walk from the doorstep to Kett in the storeroom (the cabin's revenge): the shack's own space [x, z]; every leg clear of `kept_clear`'s furniture and over nothing but the door's flat planks. The build's test walks it ten times with the door kicked in (#1091's must).

light._doc: dim: the one small window, the door and the cracks between the boards (the boards' gaps let light through: `siding` gaps)

dressing._doc: Kit props by the prop lab (PARTS.md). NEW kit the prop lab makes first (#1091's build issue lists them): bunk_stacked, bunk, plank_bench, saddle, saddle_rack, bedroll, skillet, tin_plate, tin_cans, gun_belt, bridle. Existing: box_stove, coffeepot, table, whiskey_bottle, beer_bottle, card_deck, crate, shelves, coat_pegs, flour_sack, coffee_mill, tin_cup, oil_lamp, rope_coil, folded_blanket.

L1.use: two bunks one over the other along the west wall from the front corner: clear of the door's swing and the lane
a single plank bunk along the east wall under the window
a sixth man's, rolled against the east wall between the bunk and the stove
rough plank table down the room's middle, east of the lane
the sheet-iron box stove in the SE corner on flat stones, its pipe up through the roof
a board shelf on the back wall east of the storeroom's door (high)
a crate of empty cans and bottles out under the lean-to (the stand-ins left no room by the stove)
a gun belt, a coat and a bridle on the east wall's pegs
clothes on the west wall past the bunks (high, over the lane)

S1.use: the storeroom's back wall, east half: tins, ammunition boxes, a lantern
spare tack on the east wall

L2.use: in the lean-to: a pole rail with three saddles and blankets
split juniper firewood (a woodpile kit if the prop lab has one by then)

wear._why: five rough men a year in it, boots and spurs, nothing swept

boards._why: rough mill boards gone grey-brown (the homestead barn's rough class)

rough._why: weathered silver-tan, as the homestead's shakes (#1160)

sandstone._why: the footing stones and the doorstep (a red sandstone wants its own entry later)

sources: Fred T. Hodgson, Practical Carpentry (1883): board-and-batten on a light frame, common rafters, shingle lath.
Eric Sloane, An Age of Barns (1967): vertical board siding, battens, batten doors.
USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-282, 2021): spans of the sleepers and rafters.
Line camps: Richard W. Slatta, Cowboys of the Americas (1990), the line rider's shack.
